study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative models pre-trained on cross-sectional data to evaluate intra-individual longitudinal changes in neuroimaging data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used a pre-trained normative model (lifespan_58K_82_sites from Rutherford et al.) trained on 58,836 participants across 82 sites. For the clinical application, the authors used an in-house longitudinal dataset from the Early Stages of Schizophrenia study, acquired at the National Institute of Mental Health in Klecany, Czech Republic (single site, Siemens MAGNETOM Prisma 3T).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The pre-trained model used for adaptation was the lifespan_58K_82_sites"; "The clinical data used for the analysis were part of the Early Stages of Schizophrenia study"; "the original models were fit on a large dataset consisting of 58,836 participants scanned across 82 sites"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: RehakBuckova2025.pdf.md: 2.3 Preprocessing and Analysis, L269; 2.2.1 Early stages of schizophrenia patients, L243; 2.1.1 Original model for cross-sectional data, L115

answer.None (Pre-Trained NM): pre-trained normative model for cortical thickness and subcortical volumes (used as-is, not re-trained)

answer.Early Stages of Schizophrenia: site-specific adaptation of the pre-trained model (subset of healthy controls); estimation of measurement noise variance for z-diff computation (subset of healthy controls); clinical application — evaluation of longitudinal change in schizophrenia patients

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The pre-trained lifespan_58K_82_sites model was used without re-training. From the Early Stages of Schizophrenia dataset, 67 healthy controls were available after QC: a subset (33 controls) was used for site-specific adaptation and noise variance estimation, and the remaining held-out controls served as a comparison group. The 98 patients were evaluated for longitudinal change using z-diff scores.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The pre-trained model used for adaptation was the lifespan_58K_82_sites"; "We analysed data from 98 patients in the early stages of schizophrenia (38 females) and 67 controls (42 females)"; "we used the data of 33 healthy controls which were originally used for the site-specific adaptation ... and computed their z-diff scores"

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The pre-trained normative model was fit on 58,836 participants across 82 sites. A subset of 24,000 participants was used for validation, but the exact training-only N is not reported in this paper. The local dataset contributed 67 healthy controls for site adaptation and noise estimation (not for normative model training). Of these, 33 were used for adaptation/noise estimation, and the remainder were held out.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "the original models were fit on a large dataset consisting of 58,836 participants scanned across 82 sites. Specifically, cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were modelled, and the models were validated against a subset of 24,000 participants, the quality of which were was checked manually"

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The pre-trained model (lifespan_58K_82_sites) covers the human lifespan, but this paper does not report specific age statistics (mean, sd, median, range) for the 58,836 participants used to train the model. These details are in the referenced Rutherford et al. paper. The local dataset (controls) had median age 29 (18–54), but these were not used for normative model training.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "the original models were fit on a large dataset consisting of 58,836 participants scanned across 82 sites"; "Age, median (min, max), years ... Controls: 29 (18, 54)"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The sex distribution of the 58,836 participants in the pre-trained normative model is not reported in this paper. For the local dataset, 67 controls included 42 females (63%) and 25 males (37%), but these were used for site adaptation only, not for normative model training.
